visualLanguage: design_system/public/PUBLIC_UI.md. The KB-era index.html that used to sit in this directory was DELETED 2026-08-27: it was retired as a visual target on 2026-08-26 and kept only because ci:mockup-coverage required a parity.json beside any index.html, which is a gate keeping a dead file alive. The target is the patterns in PUBLIC_UI.md, built from components/site/v3. THIS FILE STILL BINDS: requiredComponents is what stops a page silently losing a section, and ci:mockup-parity reads it with or without a mockup.
competitiveTarget: Beat generic buyer-intent pages: live MLS search as the next step, a specific process walkthrough, buyer strategy sub-pages, and a listing-alerts ask. Zero invented stats. Above the fold at 1440x900 the page answers 'what is the market doing' with sourced figures and shows a real listing, which is where the portal search pages are beaten: they show inventory but no trace, no as-of date, and no broker.

Every other Stage caller renders byte-identically -- proved by diffing /sell's Stage region HTML before and after.

INVENTORY VARIANT (SITE-46, 2026-09-09): this Stage passes `inventory`, so it carries a navy band across the base of the hero holding three live figures from the Central Oregon region row of market_pulse_live -- houses for sale, median asking price, days to an offer -- each a door into the surface that publishes that same figure, under one section 0 trace with its as-of stamp. app/buy/_v3/buy-hero-inventory.ts turns the row into those props and withholds any figure it cannot source; fewer than two and the Stage is the quiet photo form again. tasteReview.beats: Against Zillow's Bend search (zillow.com/bend-or/) this fold wins provenance: 1,550 single-family houses, $749,900, 29 days to an offer, live MLS through Oregon Data Share, as of Sep 9, 2026, before anyone has searched. It loses the job: Zillow puts a priced house in the first screen; this page puts a roof.

defects.finding: The Field that breaks the fold is a crop of roof and sky with no price, address, or type chip in the first viewport, so live inventory is a caption in the Stage and not a house you can buy.

The fold is still the generic brokerage cover: owned Cascade photo, tracked eyebrow, serif H1, one button, then three facts. SITE-77 joined the facts with middots; it did not give the live market a form a reader would screenshot.
At 375 the claimed one sentence restacks as three number rows with trailing middots stranded at the line ends, which is the KPI-grid silhouette the pass said it retired.

The three figures are off-page links with no rest-state caret, underline, or hover evidence in the still, so the only data section in the fold does not reward a tap or hover with more data on this screen.
The closed source still prints the whole population sentence because the trace is middot-joined, so at 375 four lines of methodology sit between the figures and the house.
$749,900 half the houses ask more is still a fragment that leans on the numeral to finish its meaning, the KPI tell in sentence clothing.

tasteReview.rebaselineReason: evaluatorModel and shotsHash differ: SITE-46's 60 was claude-sonnet-5 on the three-tile inventory band; this mark is grok-4.6 on new first-viewport shots after SITE-77 made the band one sourced sentence. Same rubricVersion v1-2026-09-08.
tasteReview.verdict: This is not better than a 60. Killing the three-tile grid left the same cover with a sourced ticker, and at 375 that ticker is three KPI rows again. The Field still arrives as an unlabeled roof, so a buyer gets provenance without a house.
